refined_question: Let Diff0(D2, ∗) denote the group of smooth orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the 2-disk D2 that fix a marked point ∗ (for example, the origin). Is the real vector space of homogeneous quasimorphisms φ: Diff0(D2, ∗) → R one-dimensional? Here, “homogeneous quasimorphism” means a map φ with bounded defect sup_{g,h}|φ(gh)-φ(g)-φ(h)|<∞ and satisfying φ(g^n)=nφ(g) for every g∈Diff0(D2, ∗) and every n∈Z.
justification: The draft clearly targets Sam Nariman’s Question 3.2 in §3.1, not a broader neighboring problem. The paragraph immediately before Question 3.2 defines the group Diff0(D2, ∗) and notes that the difference of two bounded Euler classes gives a nontrivial quasimorphism on that group. The paragraph immediately after Question 3.2 compares this with the closed annulus case Diff0(A), where the corresponding space is known to be one-dimensional. This context shows that the intended problem is exactly whether all homogeneous quasimorphisms on Diff0(D2, ∗) are exhausted by a one-dimensional space, and the only real deficiencies in the draft are lack of self-contained definitions and a spelling correction. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
